read: A thin 24 hours. US markets were shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving and trade a half day today, and nothing cleared the Tier 1 bar. The most important item for share prices is a delay, not a decision. The FDA pushed Vertex's povetacicept (IgAN) out to 28 February after treating a late-cycle response as a major amendment, and VRTX fell about 7% after hours on Wednesday from a 52-week high. The recent run of early FDA actions has not removed late-cycle risk. In Europe, Bachem fell 12% on a capex-heavy plan to 2031, a sign that investors want proof that peptide capacity spending will pay back, even with GLP-1 demand behind it. China-originated I&I assets keep producing data: Almirall and Simcere's Treg-biased IL-2 mutein hit its Phase 2 endpoint in atopic dermatitis, but they released no effect sizes. Tone is unchanged from Wednesday: selectively risk-on, with no new XBI print since Wednesday's 156.60 (-0.14%).

items.headline: Vertex: FDA extends the povetacicept (IgAN) review by up to three months, to 28 February 2027
items.detail: The FDA classed Vertex's answer to a late-cycle information request as a major amendment; Vertex was told on 24 November, six days before the 30 November PDUFA date. VRTX fell about 7.3% after hours on Wednesday after touching a 52-week high of $571.75. Vertex did not say what the FDA asked for. An October citizen petition is asking for mandatory immunoglobulin monitoring on any label, a possible BAFF/APRIL class-labelling issue. The asset came from the $4.9bn Alpine buy and is Vertex's first nephrology launch.

items.headline: Almirall (BME: ALM) and Simcere (HKEX: 2096): SIM0278, an IL-2 mutein, meets the primary endpoint in Phase 2 atopic dermatitis
items.detail: 184 patients on three subcutaneous doses or placebo. Two doses were significant on EASI percent change at week 16, IGA 0/1 was significant, one dose was significant on EASI-90, and EASI-75 improved only numerically. No effect sizes or p-values were given. The study runs to week 52. China-originated asset licensed to Almirall in 2022 for $15m upfront.

items.headline: Pharming pauses Ruconest manufacturing after a media-fill failure at its fill-finish contractor, and warns of a likely US supply interruption
items.detail: Ruconest is about 80% of Pharming's revenue (Q3 sales $93.8m, up 14%), almost all from the US. Current US supply lasts until mid-December, and production will not restart until the root cause is fixed and the process is requalified. It raises a near-term revenue hole and possible share-loss risk in acute HAE.

items.headline: Bachem falls about 12% after its Capital Markets Day: it targets 15-18% annual sales growth to 2031 and capex of 25-30% of sales
items.detail: Growth runs from a CHF695m 2025 base, with a 33-35% EBITDA margin target (versus 28.5% in 2025). Capex is focused on Bubendorf, Sisslerfeld and new US capacity, and R&D spend rises roughly fourfold to about CHF40m. Bachem is a peptide supplier to Lilly and Novo; the sell-off shows doubts about how quickly GLP-1-linked capacity spending earns a return.

items.headline: MHRA approves NewAmsterdam / Menarini's obicetrapib (Ubeslo) and obicetrapib/ezetimibe (Evlarco) in the UK
items.detail: LDL-C fell 36% and 33% versus placebo in two 52-week trials. Follows the EU approval in September; the value-defining event is still PREVAIL, the CV outcomes trial.

items.headline: AstraZeneca is reportedly cutting up to 20% of its China community sales team
items.detail: China sales are falling while AZ keeps buying Chinese innovation. AZ neither confirmed nor denied the cuts.

items.headline: RisCura: China-origin assets made up 51% of big-pharma licensing deals with $50m+ upfronts in January-September 2026 (39% in 2025)
items.detail: Chinese biotechs took 65% of upfront capital, up from 36%.
